title: Do GRA stipends have FICA withheld

entries.query_str: do grad students pay FICA on a GRA stipend? my w-2 box 4 is 0 and i want to know if thats right before i file
entries.answer:
That can be correct. Under the **student FICA exception**, wages paid by a college or university to a student who is enrolled and regularly attending classes at that school are generally **exempt from Social Security and Medicare taxes** [1][2]. Most universities apply it to graduate research and teaching assistants who are enrolled at least half-time.

So Box 4 (Social Security tax withheld) and Box 6 (Medicare) showing 0 is expected if you were enrolled during the pay periods. Things that can change it:
- **Summer months** when you weren't enrolled — some schools withhold FICA for those pay periods [2].
- Being classified as a **full-time employee** rather than a student employee.

The stipend is still subject to **federal and state income tax** (Boxes 1, 2, 16, 17) [1].

entries.query_str: so i dont need to do anything special, just enter the w-2 as is
entries.answer: Correct — enter the W-2 as issued. Tax software will use Box 1 for wages and Box 2 for federal withholding; zeros in Boxes 4 and 6 don't need an explanation [1]. Only if you think FICA *should* have been withheld (or was withheld wrongly), contact payroll for a corrected W-2c rather than adjusting it yourself [1].
